chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
I am the leader of the believers, while wealth is the leader of the wicked.

key_terms.الْفُجَّار: The wicked, impious, or ungodly people
key_terms.يَعْسُوب: Leader, chief, or one who leads the way

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the leader of believers and the leader of the wicked according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this famous aphorism from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of 'Ya'sub' (a leader or chief) to contrast the spiritual authority of the righteous with the material dominance of the corrupt. This distinction underscores the Shia theological view that true leadership is defined by piety and divine connection, whereas the 'fujjar' (wicked) are enslaved by their accumulation of wealth, which becomes their ultimate master and source of identity.
